method_fidelity_checklist.task_named_approach: Machine learning-guided de novo design using RFR and GP models with Bayesian optimization

original_method_definition.source: Data-Driven De Novo Design of Super-Adhesive Hydrogels (referenced in data/README.md)
original_method_definition.core_algorithm: SMBO (Sequential Model-Based Optimization) with Expected Improvement acquisition
model_pairs: RFR-RFR: Random Forest as both hypothetical value provider and EI maximizer
RFR-GP: RFR as hypothetical value provider, GP as EI maximizer
GP-GP: GP as both provider and maximizer
GP-RFR: GP as provider, RFR as maximizer

assumptions: Adhesive strength is the primary optimization objective
Composition-performance relationship is learnable from limited data
Bayesian optimization efficiently explores composition space
invariants: Six monomer types define composition space
Each formulation has a single adhesive strength measurement (Glass kPa max)
Optimization proceeds in rounds with cumulative dataset growth
non_negotiable_structural_steps: Train surrogate model (RFR or GP) on current dataset
Compute Expected Improvement over composition space
Iterate until convergence or budget exhaustion

what_was_implemented: Random Forest Regressor training and evaluation
Gradient Boosting Regressor training and evaluation
Correlation analysis between compositions and strength
Optimization method comparison using existing results
what_was_approximated: Bayesian optimization itself was not re-run; analysis uses pre-computed optimization results from datasets
GP models were not explicitly trained (focused on tree-based models)

deviations_and_rationale.deviation: Did not re-run SMBO optimization loop
deviations_and_rationale.rationale: Task focuses on analyzing existing optimization results and extracting design principles rather than generating new formulations; datasets contain complete optimization trajectories from rounds 1-3

deviations_and_rationale.deviation: Used Gradient Boosting as additional model
deviations_and_rationale.rationale: Provides complementary feature importance perspective; not a deviation from task goals as original work also compared multiple ML approaches
